EFFECTIVE CHANGE (single factor relative to the imported RL baseline): robot + reference. The admitted task_feasible_effort solve is engineering-blocked (5784519: PERFORMANCE_REQUIRES_NUMERICALLY_TASK_FEASIBLE_REMATERIALIZED_START - no numerically task-feasible re-materialized start exists for any candidate here), a solver-start precondition rather than a mathematical result; the task_gap substeps=4 solve (134662a2 -> 56b45d79) converged normally (exitflag 1, 38 iterations, scaled violation 3.3e-12, objective 0). Both evaluations are publicly read complete deterministic episodes (35 actions, 700 physics steps, holding coverage complete, no numerical failure). AGENT CONTRIBUTION (not a physical or global claim): (1) I identified the S5.8 position-pass/speed-fail pattern as a state-visibility limit of the 24-state reduced model, not an integration or authority limit - the substeps=4 plan still returns objective 0 (exact predicted stop) while at the archived physical state cell rates reach 0.73 rad/m/s and the projected model's tip speed is 0.0028 m/s against 0.0426 measured (15x), with archived plan predictions 15-600x optimistic in speed yet accurate in position; (2) using the frozen prototype data (bending viscosity 5e-4 N m^2 s, section- and density-derived rho*A) I showed the Kelvin-Voigt free-decay rate eta*beta^4/(2 rho A L^4) is independent of Young's modulus and that segment_0 length is reach-bounded (target chord 0.2948 m vs 0.305 m total), so neither admitted structural variable can supply the >=2.1x (best archived NMPC 0.042 m/s) to >=3.5x (best RL 0.070 m/s) reduction required while measured speed needs 2-25x; (3) I derived the implied precision (approximately 0.4 mm tip amplitude, 0.14% of the 0.29 m travel, sustained over six consecutive 10 ms samples given tau ~ 0.15 s) and showed instantaneous_braking_v1 gives large one-step braking authority at an archived state (minimum v.a = -40.2 m^2/s^3 inside the 8 N box, 8/8/0/0 N locally optimal), so the gap is identification and precision, not actuation; (4) I tested the three admitted levers empirically - a fresh mechanics plan, two fresh PPO stages with two independent evaluations, and a 10x reward re-balance - and the re-balance bought 2.6x on holding speed (0.33966 -> 0.12967 m/s) while pushing terminal and holding position error to 0.01668/0.01675 m, i.e. the two constraints are traded against each other rather than met together; the flat, unusable critic (explained_variance ~0) shows the advantage estimates driving those updates carried essentially no return information, so the failure is not attributable to the reward weight alone. PHYSICAL SUCCESS: none - no fresh complete passing independent physical result exists in this study; nothing here is a repeatability, robustness, hardware or real-time claim, and scope is one seed-17 deterministic fixed-initial-state episode per evaluation. ESTABLISHED vs UNKNOWN: established - on frozen Design B the best achieved holding speeds are 0.042 m/s (archived NMPC) and 0.052-0.070 m/s (imported residual PPO) against a 0.020 m/s limit, and speed-emphasised runs also breach the 0.010 m holding position limit; unknown - whether a controller with an accurate 48-DOF model or identified damping law, a much larger learning budget, a working critic, or design freedom outside the two selected variables (routing radius, cell count, distal-segment stiffness, tendon count) could meet the constraint. This STOP reports failure to find a feasible robot/control within the admitted budget and variables; it does not assert infeasibility, does not claim mathematics failed, and consumes none of the 8 remaining physical launches because every remaining admitted route reduces to a physical class already measured (plan-class executions held 0.105 and 0.336 m/s, and the model-blind NMPC cannot target the failing metric).
input.stopping_condition: STOP seals the study: no further training stage (2 of 2 used, both publicly read), no further evaluation episode (reserved episodes spent), no resubmission of the engineering-blocked task_feasible_effort solve, and no physical launch of a plan class whose execution is already measured. The rule set before the expensive experiments is applied literally - fidelity plan, then full-state feedback, then the reward re-balance; each was executed once and each failed the frozen acceptance, so the study closes with a reasoned negative result rather than further repeats. A passing fresh complete independent physical result would instead have been read and selected immediately with zero confirmation.
input.weakening_observation: The hypothesis is rejected for this budget by every decisive observation: the substeps=4 task-gap plan predicted an exact stop (objective 0) instead of a realistic holding speed, so finer model resolution did not reveal the residual; both fresh independent evaluations failed (0.33966 m/s with holding position 0.01294 m; 0.12967 m/s with terminal/holding position 0.01668/0.01675 m); both publicly read training summaries end with explained_variance 5.4e-7 and 0.0 and approx_kl 0.168/0.178 against clip_range 0.2, so the advantage signal was effectively uninformative rather than merely sample-starved; and the reward re-balance that improved holding speed 2.6x simultaneously broke the position limit, indicating a genuine trade-off at this structure rather than a missing weight.
